clauses: Report the signed difference: type average minus the mean of the per-type averages.
Report the absolute difference: distance from the mean of the per-type averages, never negative.
readings: Match each budget line to its event (`budget.link_to_event` = `event.event_id`, dropping lines with no matching event). Leaving out lines where `spent` is 0, give the following for each event `type`: the average ratio of `spent` to `amount` across its budget lines (ignoring missing values), and how far that average is from the mean of the per-type averages. Report the signed difference: type average minus the mean of the per-type averages.

Match each budget line to its event (`budget.link_to_event` = `event.event_id`, dropping lines with no matching event). Leaving out lines where `spent` is 0, give the following for each event `type`: the average ratio of `spent` to `amount` across its budget lines (ignoring missing values), and how far that average is from the mean of the per-type averages. Report the absolute difference: distance from the mean of the per-type averages, never negative.
queries:
WITH type_avg AS (
    SELECT e.type AS type,
           AVG(CAST(b.spent AS REAL) / b.amount) AS avg_ratio
    FROM budget b
    JOIN event e ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id
    WHERE b.spent <> 0
    GROUP BY e.type
)
SELECT type,
       avg_ratio,
       avg_ratio - (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) FROM type_avg) AS diff
FROM type_avg;
WITH type_avg AS (
    SELECT e.type AS type,
           AVG(CAST(b.spent AS REAL) / b.amount) AS avg_ratio
    FROM budget b
    JOIN event e ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id
    WHERE b.spent <> 0
    GROUP BY e.type
)
SELECT type,
       avg_ratio,
       ABS(avg_ratio - (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) FROM type_avg)) AS diff_from_mean
FROM type_avg;
